claims.text: The initial alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
A 1–5 µm Al2O3 or Y2O3 layer is to be deposited by PVD, CVD, or a similar pack-cementation approach.
An Al2O3 coating can act as a stable oxidation-resistant layer on HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
A Y2O3 coating can act as a stable oxidation-resistant layer on HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
A dense ceramic coating limits contact between the HfNbTaTiZr substrate and oxygen at high temperature.
The stable oxide barrier restricts oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxidation can cause severe degradation of the mechanical properties of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Reducing oxygen ingress will preserve the strength and ductility of HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will reduce oxygen uptake by more than 80% relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after 100 hours in air at 1000 °C.
After coating and exposure, HfNbTaTiZr will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After coating and exposure, HfNbTaTiZr will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Uncoated HfNbTaTiZr undergoes severe oxidation and loses ductility at 1000 °C under comparable exposure conditions.
Coating efficacy may diminish above approximately 1200 °C because of spallation.
Protection beyond 300 hours or under thermal cycling remains unverified.
Long-term data on coating stability and compatibility in thermally cycled or corrosive environments are limited.

The proposed controlled experiment compares coated and uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr after 100 hours in air at 1000 °C using mass gain, room-temperature ductility, and 1000 °C yield strength as measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if coating produces no significant reduction in oxygen uptake or no improvement in retained ductility and elevated-temperature yield strength.
